## Local implementation update — 2026-10-24 (upstream review v9 resolutions)

The v9 source review found no high-severity migration regression in the native UI
library/integration gate and listed four conservative-behaviour notes plus three
strict-glyph/accessibility gaps. This update records how the concrete findings are
resolved without widening the migration contract:

* **Conservative capture identity stays.** `SurfaceGeometry` equality keeps
  `window_focused`, `minimized` and `occluded` alongside viewport, pixels-per-point
  and texture limits. Any observed focus/visibility transition can change the
  presented frame, so an admitted capture is rejected rather than re-used; the
  struct's documentation now states this intent instead of narrowing the epoch.
* **No-op `document.switch` stays strict.** `run_switch` bumps the document epoch
  even when the requested index is already active, because the command cancels the
  active command and an external client cannot prove the switch was unobservable.
  The source records that the conservative bump is deliberate.
* **Invalid pass geometry invalidates the retained surface.** `note_pass_geometry`
  now mirrors `note_raw_geometry`: a pass that cannot report a finite positive
  pixels-per-point clears `capture_geometry` and bumps both epochs. Previously the
  previous surface survived and a later admission could bind to stale geometry.
* **MTEXT Diameter is painted, not shaped.** U+2300 is absent from egui's bundled
  Proportional/Monospace/emoji faces and from the web font set. The toolbar button
  now paints CADCraft's own circle-and-slash glyph and carries the semantic name
  "Diameter"; the document text still uses U+2300, which the drafting font covers.
* **Affected controls are named.** The MTEXT height `DragValue` gets the AccessKit
  name "Text height" (its tooltip alone is not a name), and QuickCalc's conversion
  `Value` field is associated with its visible label and a meaningful placeholder
  instead of the unexplained "1".
* **Strict bundled-font regressions.** Focused kittest regressions render the
  Diameter button, MTEXT height field and QuickCalc value row with bundled
  `FontDefinitions` only (no `theme::install_fonts` system prepend), the default
  `MissingGlyphPolicy::Panic` and accessibility checks. No global tofu policy or
  accessibility opt-out is introduced.

The first macOS native-menu poll now refreshes enablement immediately by
initializing that timer to `f64::NEG_INFINITY`; `now_ms` starts near zero, so the
former `0.0` sentinel suppressed the first ~300 ms of enablement.

This amendment is source-only: it does not claim a cargo, fmt, clippy, test, wasm,
Windows/macOS or GUI result. Publication still requires fresh explicit approval
after the parent's own validation.

### Full MTEXT toolbar font regression

The bundled-font check also covers the entire formatting toolbar: alignment, list and tab
marks are drawn with original geometry, and the color button relies on egui’s menu affordance
instead of an uncovered arrow character. The font and color controls publish semantic names.
The whole-toolbar harness retains strict missing-glyph and accessible-name checks, so a system
font cannot hide an unsupported toolbar character. Native visual review remains required.


## Native MTEXT insertion follow-up (2026-10-24)

Native Wayland job29 exercised real keyboard circle creation and MTEXT entry, the
Diameter button, callback screenshot, save, normal quit, restart and reopen. The
new entities and exact `Migration 0.37 ⌀` text survive DXF reopening. The editor
showed tofu for U+2300 even though its toolbar icon was already painted correctly.
A bounded original circle/slash `GlyphRasterizer` now supplies only U+2300 when no
installed font covers it; it keeps the stored Unicode character and cursor indexes
unchanged and works without optional font files on native/web. Font setup installs
it idempotently. A real toolbar-click/TextEdit test uses the strict bundled-font
harness and checks inserted contents and caret. Job30 validates this follow-up;
fresh native visual confirmation and review remain pending.

### File-format parity

# File-format parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-25 · **Change:** minor (LAYOUT SAveas writes a layout as a DWT template) · **Target:** Autodesk AutoCAD 2027

Every format AutoCAD 2027 reads or writes, with CADCraft's support, fidelity and tests. Work
items are in [gaps.md](gaps.md#file-formats); the weighted score feeds
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md).

**Headline (estimated):** file formats ≈ **30%** of AutoCAD's. Opening the commonest 2D DXF/DWG
drawings works, but saving is lossy: everything CADCraft doesn't model is dropped, and no test
uses a real third-party file. DXF and DWG save at 2000–2018 (2018 by default, #421). Remaining: **≈ 170–280 Opus 5.5 hours**:
≈ 40–60 h for DXF/DWG fidelity (the part that decides beta), ≈ 110–180 h for the other formats
below, and ≈ 20–40 h for 3D exchange formats that wait for 3D modelling.

## How this was measured

- CADCraft: read from `crates/dxf`, `crates/io` (`dxf_read.rs`, `dxf_write.rs`, `pdf.rs`,
  `svg.rs`, `tests.rs`) and `crates/dwg` on 2026-10-10. Nothing was run (the measurement pass
  did no builds).
- AutoCAD: the formats in its Open/Save As/Import/Export/Attach/Plot dialogs, from Autodesk's
  published documentation and the menu tree in `xtask/data/menu-catalog.txt`. The installed
  AutoCAD 2027 for Mac bundle was inspected by listing names only (clean-room rule: nothing
  inside it is read): `Resources/Support` lists `acad.lin`, `acadiso.lin`, `acad.pat`,
  `acadiso.pat`, `acad.mln`, `.dct` spell dictionaries, `.pss` and `.shx` files, which confirms the
  supporting formats below exist in the target. None of them may be copied.
- No AutoCAD-produced file is committed or used as a fixture. A real-file corpus needs owner
  action (see [gaps.md](gaps.md)): files made by people who license them to us, kept in a
  separate `storytold/cadcraft-corpus` repo.

## DWG, version by version

AutoCAD 2027 opens every DWG version from R2.0 onward and saves 2018 (AC1032, still the current
DWG format), 2013, 2010, 2007, 2004, 2000 and R14. CADCraft reads DWG by converting it to DXF
with the `acadrust` 0.6.3 crate and reading that DXF; it saves by writing its own R2000 DXF and
converting it to a DWG of the chosen version (#421): SAVEAS `version`, else the drawing's own
version (the file's `$ACADVER`, 2018 for a new drawing), at least 2004 unless 2000 is asked for.
The bridge repairs two acadrust 0.6.3 gaps in 2010+ DWG: merged table cells and table-style
title/header suppression.

| DWG version | Code | AutoCAD 2027 | CADCraft read | CADCraft write | Tested how |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1.0–R2.6, R9, R10, R11/R12 | MC0.0–AC1009 | read | **no** (`is_dwg` accepts only `AC10xx` magic; acadrust doesn't target pre-R13) | no | — |
| R13 | AC1012 | read | acadrust claims support; untested | no | none |
| R14 | AC1014 | read, write | acadrust claims support; untested | **no** | none |
| 2000–2002 | AC1015 | read, write | yes via bridge | yes, when asked for (no true colours, transparency or table styles: the format has none) | synthetic round trips (`dwg_at_every_version_reads_back`, `dwg_roundtrip_keeps_non_ascii_text`) |
| 2004–2006 | AC1018 | read, write | via bridge | yes | `dwg_at_every_version_reads_back`, `dwg_roundtrip_keeps_extension_data` |
| 2007–2009 | AC1021 | read, write | via bridge | yes | `dwg_at_every_version_reads_back` |
| 2010–2012 | AC1024 | read, write | via bridge | yes | `dwg_at_every_version_reads_back`, `ac1024_dwg_with_many_entities_opens` |
| 2013–2017 | AC1027 | read, write | via bridge | yes | `dwg_at_every_version_reads_back` |
| 2018–2027 | AC1032 | read, write (default) | via bridge; untested on real files | yes (default for new drawings) | `dwg_at_every_version_reads_back` (synthetic only) |
| Web build | — | — | **no** (error: "save as DXF") | no | — |

Everything lost in the DXF read/write paths below is also lost through DWG, plus whatever
`acadrust`'s own DXF output omits (proxy objects, ACIS data, custom objects: not measured). User
report #57: a 10 MB DWG failed after about two minutes; limits now stop runaway conversions
early (#175), but the throughput problem remains. DGN line style components that no line style
definition uses (leftovers of DGN imports, hundreds of thousands in some drawings) are left out
on read with a note, so such files no longer exceed the DXF limit (#1482). **DWG ≈ 30% read,
≈ 15% write.**

## DXF, version by version

| DXF version | AutoCAD 2027 | CADCraft read | CADCraft write |
|---|---|---|---|
| R12 (AC1009), ASCII | read, write | yes: no version gating; old-style POLYLINE/VERTEX read (polyface meshes flattened to 3D polylines) | **no** |
| R12 binary | read, write | **no** (binary parser expects R13+ 2-byte group codes) | no |
| R13–R2018, ASCII | read, write each of 2000/2004/2007/2010/2013/2018 | yes, one reader for all versions | yes, each of 2000–2018 (#421): R2000 structure (later versions add only optional groups) with that `$ACADVER`; UTF-8 text from 2007; no CLASS instance counts (91) |
| R13–R2018, binary | read, write | yes | yes, each of 2000–2018 (SAVEAS `binary`; a binary file stays binary on QSAVE) |
| Code pages (`$DWGCODEPAGE`, ANSI_932/936/949/950/125x) | yes | yes (#505): ASCII and binary DXF before 2007 decode from their code page (ANSI_874/932/936/949/950/1250–1258, DOS437/850/852/866, ISO 8859, Macintosh); a file that is valid UTF-8 reads as UTF-8; Johab and other DOS code pages read as ANSI_1252 (`dxf/src/codepage.rs`) | writes `\U+` escapes (#169), which is correct; declares `ANSI_1252` |
| `\U+`/`\M+` escapes | yes | yes (`\M+` since #505; Johab `\M+4` stays literal) | `\U+` yes |

### DXF content: read and write by object type

| Content | Read | Write | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, LWPOLYLINE (widths, bulges, elevation), SPLINE, RAY, XLINE | yes | yes | round-trip tests |
| POLYLINE 2D/3D | yes | yes (as LWPOLYLINE / 3D POLYLINE) | polyface and polygon meshes flattened: lossy |
| TEXT, MTEXT, ATTDEF, INSERT + ATTRIB | yes; multiline attributes (embedded MTEXT) read and drawn | yes; multiline attributes written as embedded MTEXT (DXF 2007 and later; older versions: one line) | ATTDEF prompt kept (#137) |
| DIMENSION (all 7 kinds) | yes | yes, with anonymous `*D` blocks | a reopened dimension's `*D` block is regenerated under its name, unreferenced ones dropped (#495); DIMASSOC objects written for every associated kind — linear/aligned, angular, radial/diametric, ordinate and arc length — and read back without CADCraft's xdata (#1651) |
| DIMENSION (all 7 kinds) | yes | yes, with anonymous `*D` blocks | a reopened dimension's `*D` block is regenerated under its name, unreferenced ones dropped (#495); DIMASSOC objects written; angular block text honors DIMDSEP, including per-dimension overrides (#1646) |
| DIMENSION (all 7 kinds) | yes | yes, with anonymous `*D` blocks; their text keeps the diameter sign as `%%c`, so SHX styles plot it (#1645) | a reopened dimension's `*D` block is regenerated under its name, unreferenced ones dropped (#495); DIMASSOC objects written |
| LEADER | yes | yes | |
| MULTILEADER | yes (#459) | yes, native MULTILEADER with MLEADERSTYLE (#459) | several landings per multileader are folded into one; per-object overrides and annotative scale contexts not kept |
| HATCH pattern / solid | yes | yes; associative hatches keep their boundary objects in blocks too, and the boundary carries the hatch reactor (stretched dynamic blocks drag the fill in AutoCAD) | |
| HATCH gradient | yes | yes (#162, fixes #80) | |
| SOLID, TRACE, 3DFACE | yes | yes | |
| ACAD_TABLE | yes | yes (entity + block) | |
| VIEWPORT | yes | yes; frozen-layer lists kept (#150), also as standard group 341 layer handles that other programs read | DWG: the DXF→DWG converter does not yet write group 341 (frozen layers survive a CADCraft round trip via xdata); VP layer colour overrides lost (#99, PR #197) |
| IMAGE | yes, with IMAGEDEF | yes, with IMAGEDEF and IMAGEDEF_REACTOR | no attach command or display of the picture yet (FF10) |
| WIPEOUT | yes | yes (#147, fixes #79) | |
| MLINE (+ MLINESTYLE), HELIX, TOLERANCE | yes (#510, #420) | yes | |
| REGION | other programs' REGIONs (ACIS data) kept as Unknown | our regions are written as closed polylines tagged with CADCraft xdata (#510; ACIS has no public spec) | |
| 3DSOLID, BODY, SURFACE, MESH, SHAPE, UNDERLAY, OLE2FRAME, LIGHT, CAMERA, SECTION, POINTCLOUD, proxy entities | kept as Unknown (raw tags) | written back as read, with their CLASS records (#528); a proxy entity's class number (group 91) is renumbered to its class's place in the written CLASSES (#1812); **dropped by DWG save** (acadrust) | only their layer follows edits |
| Header variables | all read | 36 written | AutoCAD writes about 280 |
| Tables: LAYER (+ transparency, description), LTYPE, STYLE, DIMSTYLE, BLOCK_RECORD | yes | yes | |
| Tables: VPORT, VIEW, UCS, APPID | yes | yes: saved viewport configurations (#504), named views, UCSs | UCS elevation lost |
| Objects: LAYOUT, DICTIONARY, XRECORD, TABLESTYLE, DIMASSOC | yes | yes | |
| Objects: GROUP, MLINESTYLE, MLEADERSTYLE, IMAGEDEF, SCALE | yes | yes (groups #417, scale list #468) | |
| Objects: VISUALSTYLE, PLOTSETTINGS, materials, field objects and other unmodelled objects | kept raw (#528) | written back as read; a proxy object (ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT) keeps its class: its group 91 is renumbered to the written CLASSES, which keep the class it names, and one whose number names no class is dropped (#1812) | not editable |
| Foreign xdata, extension dictionaries, reactors, unmodelled objects, colour books | kept raw (#528); an entity's xdata is part of the entity, so COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY and paste keep it on the copies (EXPLODE pieces don't) | written back, handles remapped, references to deleted objects dropped | through DWG: xdata on table records and blocks, entity colour books and reactors, custom-class objects lost (acadrust) |
| Objects: dynamic block data (ACAD_EVALUATION_GRAPH, BLOCK…PARAMETER, BLOCK…ACTION, grips) | read into a model (`dynblock`, `blocks.dynamic`): parameters, visibility states, value sets, stretch and lookup actions; references: their dynamic block, values and custom properties (`blocks.reference`, Properties ▸ Custom, read-only); kept raw (#528) | written back as read; a changed visibility state is written as AutoCAD writes it (a new anonymous block with its `AcDbBlockRepBTag`, the objects' `AcDbBlockRepETag`, the reference's representation data) | visibility states (and lookups that set only them) can be changed (`blocks.reference.set`, Properties ▸ Custom); distances, positions and the actions they drive not yet; DWG open and save keep it too (checked with an AutoCAD dynamic block) |
| Handles and owners | entity handles kept; others regenerated | consistent | stable across CADCraft re-saves (#495); other programs' table and object handles renumbered once |

**DXF ≈ 50% read, ≈ 30% write** (estimated; weights: common 2D entities 50%, annotation objects
20%, tables/objects 15%, foreign data preservation 15%).

## Other formats

| Format | AutoCAD 2027 | CADCraft | Hours to parity (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DWT templates | open, save | NEW/QNEW from `.dwt` and `.dxf` templates, SAVEAS `.dwt` (#552); LAYOUT SAveas writes one layout and the named objects it uses as a `.dwt` (`layout.saveas`) | 0–1 |
| DWS standards | open, save, CHECKSTANDARDS | no | 6–10 |
| PDF output (PLOT, EXPORTPDF) | multi-sheet, layers, searchable text, hyperlinks | vector PDF with lineweights, real text in embedded TrueType subsets, layers (OCG), several sheets per file and hyperlinks (#567, #571); object transparency as PDF alpha when "Plot transparency" is on (the option isn't saved in DXF/DWG: no public plot layout flag) | 1–2 |
| PDF import (PDFIMPORT) and PDF underlays (PDFATTACH) | yes | no | 15–25 |
| Raster images attach (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP …) | yes | IMAGE entity exists, no attach/loading/display path | 6–10 |
| PNG / JPEG / BMP / TIFF export | PNGOUT, JPGOUT, BMPOUT, TIFOUT | PNG; SVG too (AutoCAD doesn't export SVG) | 1–2 |
| DWF/DWFx export, DWF underlay | yes | no | 10–15 |
| DGN import/export/underlay | yes | no (needs a public spec; owner decision) | 25–40 |
| WMF, EPS, ACIS SAT, STL, FBX, IGES/STEP (Windows), 3DS | various | no; most are 3D and wait for M11 | 20–40 |
| SHX fonts (`.shx`, big fonts) | read | **not parsed**: our stroke font or FONTALT stands in, so text metrics differ from AutoCAD | 8–12 |
| Linetype (`.lin`) and hatch pattern (`.pat`) files | load user files | user files load (#552); linetype shape (SHX) elements are skipped | 1–2 |
| Plot styles (`.ctb`, `.stb`), plotter configs (`.pc3`), `.pmp` | yes | plot style tables in our own JSON format ([plot-styles.md](plot-styles.md)) and kept in the drawing; plotter devices with papers and printable areas in our own JSON format ([plotters.md](plotters.md), #564); binary `.ctb`/`.stb`/`.pc3`/`.pmp` not read (no public spec) | 4–8 |
| Scripts (`.scr`) | SCRIPT | script text through the CLI, MCP and control channel; no SCRIPT command reading a `.scr` file | 1–2 |
| Aliases (`.pgp`), CUI(x), workspaces | yes | user alias files and ALIASEDIT (#552); no CUI(x) or workspaces | 4–8 |
| SVG import (`.svg`, `.svgz`) | yes (via scripts) | OPEN reads shapes, paths, groups and Inkscape layers into entities (#636); no CSS classes, `use`, fills, text or images (what the drawing loses is named in a note on open, #627) | 2–4 |
| AutoLISP (`.lsp`, `.fas`, `.vlx`), `.dll`/`.arx` plug-ins | yes | `.lsp` loads (APPLOAD, `(load)`, a dropped file; #758); no Visual LISP ActiveX (`vlax-`), DCL dialogs or reactors; `.fas`/`.vlx` are compiled and undocumented; no `.dll`/`.arx` | see [gaps.md](gaps.md) (E1) |
| Data extraction (`.csv`, `.xls`) and data links | yes | DATAEXTRACTION/EATTEXT to CSV or a table (#433); table data links read CSV (#534); no `.xls`, no `.dxe` templates | 3–5 |
| eTransmit (`.zip` packages) | yes | no | 4–6 |

## Tests

`crates/io/src/tests.rs` has 36 tests (round trips of entities, styles, associativity, tables,
constraints, non-ASCII text, DWG round trips, hostile input). **All inputs are synthetic**:
inline strings or our own writer's output. No test opens a file made by another program, and no
external validator runs in CI (ezdxf's audit was run by hand once, 2026-10-06). The next step is
a licensed real-file corpus with an open → save → re-open → compare test per file, and checking
our output in AutoCAD black-box.

## Revision history

| Date | Change | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-25 | minor | LAYOUT SAveas (`layout.saveas`) writes a layout as a drawing template: its page setup and paper space objects, no model space objects or other layouts, and only the named objects they use |
| 2026-10-22 | minor | DXF/DWG save: angular, diametric and radial dimensions get standard DIMASSOC objects (one centre reference to the circle for radial/diametric, the definition points for angular), so AutoCAD follows their geometry; the standard objects of those kinds are read back too, without CADCraft's xdata (#1651) |
| 2026-10-19 | minor | DXF/DWG save: angular dimension block text honors DIMDSEP, including per-dimension overrides (#1646) |
| 2026-10-19 | minor | A file's own arrowhead blocks with standard names (AutoCAD's `_Dot`, `_DotSmall`), named only by a dimension style, are kept and saved as they were instead of being replaced by CADCraft's solids; PURGE keeps arrowhead blocks dimension styles name |
| 2026-10-20 | minor | DIMENSION: the `*D` block's MTEXT, and the MTEXT EXPLODE leaves, hold the diameter sign as `%%c` instead of the decoded U+2300, which no SHX font has, so other programs plotted diameter dimensions in an SHX style without the sign (#1645) |
| 2026-10-21 | minor | Proxy objects and entities keep their class through a save: group 91 renumbered to the written CLASSES (the class it names is kept), a proxy whose number names no class dropped (#1812) |
| 2026-10-17 | minor | DWG read: DGN line style components no line style definition reaches are left out before the DXF bridge, with a read note; an 83 MB site plan with 888,483 of them (1.2 GB of DXF, over the limit) now opens (#1482) |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | PDF output: object transparency plotted as PDF alpha (`/ExtGState` `/ca` `/CA`) when the page setup's or the plot's "Plot transparency" is on; PNG plots blend it, SVG uses `opacity`; plots without it are unchanged byte for byte |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | DXF/DWG save: the Model layout's plot settings are written as CADCraft plots model space, drawing extents scaled to fit (PLOTSETTINGS 74 = 1, 75 = 0), instead of plot type 5 "Layout information", which other programs' Plot dialogs can't use for model space |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | VIEWPORT frozen layers also written and read as AutoCAD's group 341 layer handles, so third-party viewers honour per-viewport freezing in DXF (DWG converter gap noted) |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | HATCH: associative hatches inside blocks keep their source objects; boundaries carry `{ACAD_REACTORS}` |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Dynamic block grips: grip objects read by graph id; a drag is saved as AutoCAD saves a Properties change |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Dynamic block references: visibility states can be changed and are saved as AutoCAD saves them |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Dynamic block references: definition, values and custom properties read (`blocks.reference`, Properties ▸ Custom) |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Dynamic block data row: parameters and actions read into a model (`blocks.dynamic`); kept by DXF and DWG save |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Multiline attributes (embedded MTEXT) read, drawn and written back instead of losing their text |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | Rows refreshed for merged work: code pages and `\M+` (#505), MULTILEADER (#459), IMAGE, MLINE/HELIX/REGION/TOLERANCE, VPORT/VIEW/UCS tables, modelled and raw objects, foreign data (#528), DWT templates and user `.lin`/`.pat`/`.pgp` files (#552), PDF output (#567, #571), plotter devices (#564), data extraction (#433, #534); weighted percentages not re-measured |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | DXF (ASCII and binary) and DWG saved at 2000–2018, 2018 by default (#421) |
| 2026-10-10 | minor | WIPEOUT and gradients written since #147/#162; other save losses remain (#201, #204, #208, #209, #213, #223) |
| 2026-10-10 | major | First file-format parity doc: DWG and DXF version by version, per-object read/write, other formats |

### Where CADCraft falls short of AutoCAD

# Where CADCraft falls short of AutoCAD

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-25 · **Change:** minor (Named Viewports dialog: U11 narrowed; MVIEW Restore and PURGE of multiline styles had landed: F15 and F21 corrected) · **Target:** Autodesk AutoCAD 2027

Every known shortfall, one row each, ranked within each section by user impact. This is the work
list: agents pick from here (top of a section first), and remove or update a row in the same PR
that closes it. Numbers and weights live in [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md); hours
are Opus 5.5 agent-hours, calibrated as explained there. "Est." means a judgement from the cited
evidence. Rows marked **[alpha blocker]** are what fails the [alpha gate](roadmap.md#alpha-gate);
do them first.

## Top 10 across everything

| # | Gap | Why it ranks here | Est. | Doc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **[alpha blocker]** **Saving DWG drops what we don't model** (DXF now writes back unknown entities and objects, foreign xdata, extension dictionaries, reactors, layer states and colour books, #528, and native MULTILEADERs, #459 (not yet tested through DWG); through DWG, acadrust drops custom-class entities and objects, xdata on table records and blocks, entity colour books and reactors) | Opening a colleague's DWG and saving it still deletes some content: the one thing a CAD user can't forgive | 6–10 | [file formats](file-format-parity.md) |
| 2 | **[alpha blocker]** **No real-file test corpus and no check in AutoCAD** | All 36 file tests are synthetic; nobody has verified a CADCraft DWG/DXF opens cleanly in AutoCAD | 10–15 + human | [file formats](file-format-parity.md#tests) |
| 3 | **Ellipse and spline geometry is tessellated** (intersections, offsets, closest points; polyline offset ignores bulges) | Coordinates are subtly wrong; offsets of ellipses come out as polylines | 30–50 | [geometry](geometry-parity.md) |
| 4 | **[alpha blocker]** **No dynamic blocks or REFEDIT; xrefs can't be edited in place or clipped** (xrefs, #525, groups, #417, and the Block Editor for static blocks landed) | Most production drawings use them | 55–90 | [features](#features) |
| 5 | **No autosave in the web build** (the desktop app has SAVETIME autosave, Drawing Recovery, AUDIT and RECOVER since #406) | Browser users lose unsaved work when the tab or the browser goes down | 3–5 | [features](#features) |
| 6 | **No CI runs the Rust tests on pull requests** (`cargo fmt` on main is fixed) | open PRs land without a gate; regressions go unseen | 2–3 | [stability](#stability) |

## Features

| # | Gap | Evidence | User impact | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **[alpha blocker]** Prompt options that still print "not available yet": -ATTEDIT one-at-a-time Position, Height, Angle and Style, colour books in -ATTEDIT Color, -RENAME of materials, plot styles and viewport configurations. SPLINEDIT Join, Edit vertex Add and Elevate order (#559), PEDIT Edit vertex and the other SPLINEDIT options (#558) done: Edit vertex Tangent directions last for the PEDIT session only (LWPOLYLINE stores none). MTEXT Dynamic/Static columns done (#547). SPLINE, MTEXT and MLEADER options done (#408): SPLINE Object fits the polyline's vertices (no spline frame is kept) (STRETCH polygon, CP and WP, and fence selection done; TRIM/EXTEND, PLINE arc mode and Length, XLINE done (#397); OFFSET, ROTATE and FILLET options done earlier) | `cmd/blocks/attedit.rs`, `cmd/props/rename.rs` | Low: the most-used commands are done | 1–3 |
| F2 | XREF editing in place and clipping: XCLIP is missing. REFEDIT, REFSET and REFCLOSE edit a block reference in place (working set, faded rest of the block, everything else locked, save or discard; #813); left: editing an xref in place (its source drawing is not written back; XOPEN opens it), picking nested references, a dimmed look for the locked drawing and a banner with Save and Discard, attribute sync of other references (ATTSYNC). XATTACH, the External References palette, -XREF (Bind/Detach/Path/Unload/Reload/Overlay), XBIND, XOPEN, overlays, relative paths and loading at open are done (#525). Unloaded state and xref-layer overrides last only for the session | `cmd/blocks/xref.rs` | Medium: xrefs can't be edited in place or clipped | 15–25 |
| F3 | **[alpha blocker]** (dynamic-block authoring is beta) No dynamic-block authoring: parameters and actions can't be added in the Block Editor. Dynamic blocks from other files are read and their references edited (visibility, distances, stretch and move, lookups, grips). BEDIT (with the Edit Block Definition dialog, which also starts new blocks), BSAVE, BSAVEAS and BCLOSE edit a static block definition, and every reference updates; REFEDIT edits a reference in place; no authoring palettes yet | issue #185 offers help | High: standard libraries are dynamic | 40–65 |
| F4 | Autosave leftovers: no autosave in the web build (browser storage); autosave files are DXF, not DWG; no separate RECOVER mode in the file readers (SAVETIME, Drawing Recovery, AUDIT and RECOVER landed with #406; AUDITCTL `.adt` log landed) | `engine/src/autosave.rs`, `engine/src/audit.rs` | Low-medium (web users) | 2–4 |
| F5 | Associative arrays (ASsociative, Levels, polar ROWs, ARRAYEDIT, ARRAYCLOSE) landed (#448); left: grip editing of arrays (count/spacing grips), ARRAYPATH is not associative, ARRAYEDIT has no item deletion (CTRL+click) and no Key point base points, levels only shift Z (no 3D view) | `cmd/array.rs`, `cmd/array/edit.rs` | Medium | 4–6 |
| F7 | Dimensions: no DIMSTYLE manager dialog; no smart DIM; DIMALTTD/DIMALTTZ, DIMUPT and DIMTXTDIRECTION not modelled; jog height and break size not style settings; DIMBREAK breaks don't follow moved objects; with DIMTFILL 1 the written `*D` block and EXPLODE keep no background mask (a WIPEOUT over the text box would), and a true-color DIMTFILLCLR is written to DXF as the nearest ACI (style variables, DIMJOGGED, DIMJOGLINE, DIMBREAK, DIMEDIT, DIMINSPECT and QDIM modes done, #507; the DIMTFILL/DIMTFILLCLR text background done) | `doc/src/tables.rs`, `cmd/annotate_dimedit.rs`, `cmd/annotate_qdim.rs` | Medium | 10–15 |
| F8 | TOLERANCE leftovers (feature control frames landed, #420: model, our own symbol drawing, DXF, command-line prompts, explode, grips): no Geometric Tolerance dialog, no LEADER/QLEADER tolerance annotation, no in-place editing of a frame's contents | `cmd/tolerance.rs` | Low-medium (mechanical) | 2–4 |
| F10 | MLEADEREDIT (add/remove leader), MLEADERALIGN and MLEADERCOLLECT landed, but a multileader has one landing and one block (a collection keeps the other blocks as block references beside it; MLEADERALIGN has no Options-menu preview); MLEADERSTYLE has 5 fields (block content and spline/no-leader types are per command, not in the style; block content has no attributes) | `annotate.rs`, `cmd/mleader_content.rs`, `tables.rs:417` | Medium | 8–12 |
| F9 | MTEXT is typed in an on-canvas editor with a formatting toolbar (font, height, bold, italic, underline, overline, colour, alignment, lists, tab and special characters) and a ruler for indents and tab stops (#532); left: the box does not lay the text out by the indents, tabs, columns or font weights while typing (bold shows wider, overline is not drawn), no justification (attachment) or columns controls in the editor, existing MTEXT cannot be edited (no DDEDIT/MTEDIT), stacked fractions and other codes show as placeholders; no fields (FIELD, UPDATEFIELD) and no spell check (SPELL): open PR #551. Paragraph indents, tabs, bullets, numbering and columns landed (#547) | `ui-egui/mtext_editor.rs`, `engine/mtext_edit.rs` | Medium | 10–18 |
| F11 | Tables (cell styles, formulas, TABLEDIT, TABLEEXPORT, table breaking and CSV data links landed, #534): formulas aren't read from or written as AutoCAD FIELD objects (other programs see values); number formats apply to formula results only; cell text doesn't wrap; custom cell styles, breaks and data links travel as CADCraft xdata (not through DWG); data links read CSV only (no Excel ranges, no write-back, not on the web); no cell-style tab in the Table Style dialog | `cmd/table/*`, `io/dxf_table.rs` | Low-medium | 6–10 |
| F12 | Annotative scaling done (#468): scale list (SCALELISTEDIT), CANNOSCALE, OBJECTSCALE, ANNOALLVISIBLE/ANNOAUTOSCALE, viewport scale, DXF, status bar list. Left: per-scale positions (ANNORESET is a no-op), a viewport annotation scale apart from its viewport scale, annotative objects inside blocks and old LEADERs, AutoCAD files' per-object scale contexts (read as not annotative) | `cmd/annoscale.rs`, `doc/src/anno.rs` | Low-medium | 4–8 |
| F14 | **[alpha blocker]** Plotting leftovers: binary `.ctb`/`.stb`/`.pc3` files can't be read; model-space PDF plots keep the default margins (a device paper's margins apply to layouts and PNG plots); no system printers (H3); the page setup's "Plot transparency" is not saved in DXF/DWG (the public DXF Reference has no plot layout flag for it), so it lasts for the session and in JSON only. The Plot dialog (#160), Plot Preview and PUBLISH (#186), plot styles (CTB and STB, [plot-styles.md](plot-styles.md), #410) with their end, join and fill styles, plotter devices with paper sizes and printable areas ([plotters.md](plotters.md), #564), and plotted transparency (page setup and Plot dialog option, PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE) landed | `io/src/plotter.rs`, `cmd/plotters.rs` | Medium | 4–8 |
| F13 | Hatch: 23 patterns (AutoCAD ~85; ours must stay original); the Hatch and Gradient and Hatch Edit dialogs have no Preview or Inherit Properties (HPDLGMODE 0 keeps HATCH on the command line); no MPolygon; HATCHEDIT and -HATCHEDIT add boundaries from picked points or closed objects and remove chosen loops, but a hatch copied with its boundary isn't linked to the copy; HPGAPTOL closes gaps between curve ends only | `doc/src/library.rs`, `cmd/hatch.rs`, `cmd/hatch/edit.rs` | Medium | 6–10 |
| F15 | Viewports: a clipped viewport and its clip boundary move and scale separately. Polygonal, object and clipped viewports, VPCLIP, MVIEW ON/OFF/Lock/2/3/4 and the status-bar scale list landed (#453), MVIEW Restore in #633 | `cmd/layout/viewports.rs` | Low | 2–4 |
| F16 | Groups: no group bounding box or single grip when a group is selected (GROUPDISPLAYMODE), copying a whole group does not make a new group, no Object Grouping dialog (GROUP, GROUPEDIT, UNGROUP, -GROUP, PICKSTYLE group selection and the DXF/DWG round trip landed, #417); PICKSTYLE's associative-hatch bit is stored but unused | `cmd/groups.rs` | Low | 2–4 |
| F17 | Attributes (ATTSYNC, global -ATTEDIT, BATTMAN editing and DATAEXTRACTION/EATTEXT landed, #433): no verify, preset or lock-position modes, and multiline attributes (read, drawn and saved since 2026-10-12) can't be created or switched in BATTMAN; data extraction covers block references and attribute values (CSV or a table) only — no wizard, nested blocks, other objects' properties, `.dxe` templates or spreadsheet output | `cmd/blocks/battman.rs`, `cmd/blocks/extract.rs` | Low | 4–6 |
| F19 | MATCHPROP Settings is a keyword prompt (no dialog) and has no material, shadow or centre-object settings; TEXTTOFRONT and HATCHTOBACK act on the current space only; OVERKILL doesn't compare polyline segments with other objects (picker and Settings, DRAWORDER Above/Under, TEXTTOFRONT, HATCHTOBACK, OVERKILL tolerance/ignore/overlap/end-to-end options landed, #439) | `props/matchprop.rs`, `draworder.rs`, `overkill.rs` | Low | 2–4 |
| F20 | OPTIONS dialog done (#23): Display, Open and Save, Drafting, Selection, User Preferences and Profiles tabs, and the user profile (object snap modes, drafting toggles, Dynamic Input, PICKBOX, APERTURE, GRIPSIZE, CURSORSIZE, PICKFIRST, PICKADD, QPMODE, model and paper background, snap marker size, system cursor) survives restarts. Left: right-click customization, the autosave interval and default save version on Open and Save (the features themselves landed, #406, #421), AutoSnap magnet and tooltip toggles, colours of the other drawing-area elements, named profiles with import and export | `ui-egui/src/options/` | Low | 2–4 |
| F21 | MLINE, REGION and HELIX are objects since #510, with gaps: MLEDIT tees trim square; UNION/SUBTRACT/INTERSECT only combine regions whose boundaries don't meet; regions are saved as closed polylines (no ACIS data) | `draw2/mline.rs`, `inquiry/regions.rs`, `dxf_region.rs` | Low | 6–10 |
| F22 | Inquiry leftovers (COUNT across spaces and nested blocks, the QuickCalc palette and COMPARE landed, #563; MASSPROP on regions, #510): COMPARE compares the tab shown, not every layout at once (COMPAREEXPORT, the comparison as a new drawing, landed); COMPAREEXPORT puts the two sets of objects in model-space groups, where AutoCAD puts them in blocks; QuickCalc keeps its history and variables for the session only | `file/compare.rs`, `palettes/quickcalc.rs` | Low | 3–5 |
| F23 | No Sheet Set Manager, eTransmit, Share, Traces, Markup Import, Activity Insights | menu items uncovered | Low-medium (team workflows) | 40–70 |
| F24 | No 3D: UCS, 3D views, orbit, solids, surfaces, meshes, sections, visual styles, materials, lights, rendering (150 menu items) | [parity-checklist](parity-checklist.md) | Medium (3D users) | 300–450 |

## UI/UX

Detail and evidence: [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md).

Outlined fill highlights now keep deterministic contour starts and directions across pointer
repaints and GPU rebuilds, preventing the dashed preview from appearing to flicker (U6).

Options ▸ Selection can now require two separate clicks for a selection window (PICKDRAG 0)
or allow clicks and drag (2, default), saved in the user profile. Drag-only mode (1) remains unavailable.
| # | Gap | User impact | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|
| U4 | Tab snap cycling offers the closest snap of each mode, not every candidate. Typed snap overrides (`END`, `MID` … `NON`), the Shift/Ctrl+right-click snap menu and Tab cycling landed (#393), the menu's Temporary track point in #441 | Low | 1 |
| U5 | Grip menus open on right-click only (no hover menu, no Ctrl to cycle the options); no multifunctional grips on dimensions, MLEADER, hatches or text; Add Vertex on an arc segment straightens it. Hot-grip options (Base point, Copy, Undo, Reference, eXit), multiple hot grips and the polyline/line/arc grip menus landed (#425) | Low-medium | 2–4 |
| U6 | Selection: lasso; the CLass keyword; isolation saved with the drawing (OBJECTISOLATIONMODE 1) and the status-bar isolate button. Press-drag windows (#63), the W, C, F, WP and CP keywords (#226), BOX, AUto, SIngle, Multiple, Group, Add, Remove and Undo, SELECTSIMILAR, ISOLATEOBJECTS/HIDEOBJECTS/UNISOLATEOBJECTS (#428) and selection cycling (#1143) landed | Medium | 3–5 |
| U7 | Right-click menus: no in-place layout tab rename or Move or Copy dialog, no Select All Layouts, no Paste to command line; palette menus are on the Layers rows and the Properties background only. The command menu (held right-click: Enter, Cancel, Recent Input, options, Snap Overrides, Pan/Zoom), the selection menu with object edits, command line, drawing tab, layout tab and palette menus landed (#512) | Low | 1–2 |
| U10 | SETVAR covers about 150 of ~1,000 variables (UNDO options, MREDO and UNDOCTL, and header variables such as CIRCLERAD, OFFSETDIST, POLYSIDES, HPNAME and the dimension variables in SETVAR ? landed, #461; typing a bare variable name as a command runs SETVAR on it) | Low-medium | 3–5 |
| U11 | VIEW Orthographic, UCS and background settings; view twist is kept but not shown (Zoom Realtime and Dynamic, ZOOMFACTOR, named views (VIEW) and tiled model viewports with saved configurations (VPORTS) landed in #463, MVIEW Restore in #633, and the Named Viewports dialog, which restores or deletes a saved configuration) | Low | 1–2 |
| U12 | Workspaces, navigation bar, CUI customisation, ViewCube drag (#7) (the Command Aliases dialog landed, #1381) | Low-medium | 13–23 |
| U13 | `.dxf` from Finder fails to open on macOS (#158) (window controls fixed, #161) | Medium | 1–2 |

## File formats

Detail: [file-format-parity.md](file-format-parity.md).

| # | Gap | User impact | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|
| FF1 | **[alpha blocker]** Round-trip what we don't model. DXF done (#528): unknown entities and objects (with their CLASS records), foreign xdata (hyperlinks included), extension dictionaries, persistent reactors, DICTIONARYVAR and XRECORDs, layer states, colour book colours, references remapped on save; IMAGE, VIEW/UCS, groups, block descriptions, true colours, transparency (#201, #204, #208, #209, #213, #223); WIPEOUT and gradients (#147, #162). Left: through DWG, acadrust drops custom-class entities and objects, xdata on table records and blocks, entity colour book names and reactors; UCS elevation; MTEXT background colours; unknown entities follow only layer edits, and renamed layers and blocks lose their foreign data | High | 6–10 |
| FF2 | Multileader leftovers (native MULTILEADER read/write landed, #459): several landings per multileader (extra leader roots are folded into the lines), per-object overrides (leader colour and linetype, arrowhead symbol, text frame), annotative scale contexts; check the text placement of our MULTILEADER output in AutoCAD | Medium | 3–5 |
| FF3 | Save-version leftovers (DXF/DWG 2000–2018, binary DXF, SAVEAS `version`/`binary` and the default save version landed, #421): no R14 DWG or R12 DXF output; the Save dialog can't pick the version per file (the file picker doesn't report the chosen type; File > Default Save Format sets it); no command-line SAVEAS format prompt | Low | 2–4 |
| FF4 | Code-page leftovers (pre-2007 DXF read in their `$DWGCODEPAGE` landed, #505): Johab (ANSI_1361) and DOS 855/857/860–865/869 read as ANSI_1252; saving declares `ANSI_1252` instead of the file's code page (the text is pure ASCII, so still correct); acadrust approximates DOS code pages in pre-2007 DWG (DOS437 as 866, DOS850 as 1252) | Low | 1–2 |
| FF5 | **[alpha blocker]** Real-file corpus (`storytold/cadcraft-corpus`), open → save → reopen tests, black-box check in AutoCAD | High | 10–15 + human |
| FF6 | **[alpha blocker]** DWG throughput: a 10 MB DWG took ~2 min to fail (#57) | High for real projects | 6–10 |
| FF7 | Table record and object handles from other programs' files are renumbered on the first save (entity handles are kept; `*D` blocks no longer duplicate and once reopened, CADCraft's own files keep every handle across saves, #495) | Low | 4–6 |
| FF8 | SHX fonts (shape and big fonts) not read | Medium-high (text metrics differ) | 8–12 |
| FF9 | `.pc3` plotter configuration files; linetype shape (SHX) elements are skipped (templates and `.dwt`, user `.lin`/`.pat` and `.pgp` alias files landed, #552; `.ctb`/`.stb`, #410) | Low-medium | 5–10 |
| FF10 | PDF import and underlays (PDFATTACH); raster image attach (IMAGEATTACH). PDF export has real text in embedded TrueType subsets, PDF layers, several sheets per file and hyperlinks (#567, #571) | Medium | 20–35 |
| FF11 | DWF/DWFx, DGN, WMF, EPS, ACIS/STL and other exchange formats | Low-medium | 50–100 |
| FF12 | DWG in the web build | Medium | 6–10 |
| FF13 | R12 binary DXF, pre-R13 DWG | Low | 10–20 |
| FF14 | SVG import leftovers (shapes, paths, groups and Inkscape layers landed, #636): no CSS classes (`<style>`), `use` references, fills and gradients, text or embedded images; rounded rectangle corners (`rx`/`ry`) are ignored. Opening such a file names what was left out (#627) | Low-medium | 2–4 |

## Ecosystem and automation

| # | Gap | Est. |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | AutoLISP beyond the core (#758 landed the language, `command`, entity lists, selection sets, `get…` input, APPLOAD, `(load)`, `c:` commands and `acad.lsp`/`acaddoc.lsp` at startup; #1820 gave APPLOAD its `.lsp` file picker): Visual LISP ActiveX (`vlax-`, `vla-`), DCL dialogs, reactors, an APPLOAD Startup Suite, UCS-aware `trans` | 26–46 |
| E3 | Express Tools equivalents (SUPERHATCH; NCOPY, BREAKLINE, TXT2MTXT, BURST and MOCORO exist: BREAKLINE's Block option takes a block of the drawing, not a `.dwg` file, and TXT2MTXT's Settings are command-line prompts rather than a dialog, without the uniform line spacing option) | 24–40 |
| E4 | Plug-in API (owner decision: Rust/WASM plug-ins rather than ObjectARX/.NET) | 30–50 |
| E5 | CUI customisation (the alias editor, ALIASEDIT's Command Aliases dialog, landed, #1381; edits stay for the session) | 13–23 |

## AI features

| # | Gap | Est. |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Smart Blocks equivalents (placement suggestions, replace, detect and convert, search), using local open models | 25–50 + model licensing |
| A2 | An in-app assistant (AutoCAD has Autodesk Assistant); CADCraft's MCP server already lets any agent drive it, including read-only structured queries of the current selection (`query_entities selected:true`) | 10–20 |
| A3 | Markup Assist (import markups from PDFs/images) | 10–20 |

### Geometry parity

# Geometry parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-22 · **Change:** minor (bounded constraint expression and parameter depth) · **Target:** Autodesk AutoCAD 2027

CAD users trust numbers: a trimmed endpoint, an offset, an intersection or an area is either right
to the last displayed digit or the tool is unusable for production drawings. This document
audits CADCraft's geometry kernel (`crates/geom`, the curve code in `crates/engine/src/cmd`,
`crates/constraints`) curve by curve against what AutoCAD users rely on. Snaps and tracking are
in [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md); dimension and hatch behaviour in [gaps.md](gaps.md).

**Headline (estimated): geometry ≈ 40% (weighted below: 41%), of which the constraint solver ≈ 50%.** Everything built
from lines, arcs and circles is exact. Ellipses and splines are handled by tessellating them, so
intersections, offsets, trims and snaps on them are approximations; polyline offsets don't
recompute arc bulges or clean up loops; tolerances are absolute, so very large or very small
drawings behave differently from mid-sized ones. 3D geometry doesn't exist. Remaining:
**≈ 90–140 Opus 5.5 hours** for 2D precision and the solver, plus the 3D kernel (M11, see
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md)).

## How this was measured

Read from the source on 2026-10-10 (main at bd2412f), with file:line evidence in the tables. No
numeric comparison against AutoCAD has been run yet: the plan is a set of synthetic drawings whose
exact answers are known analytically, measured in both apps black-box (LIST, ID, AREA results)
and in CADCraft headless. Until then the percentages are judgements.

Weights (how much AutoCAD users lean on each area in 2D drafting): numeric robustness 15%,
curve representation 10%, intersections 15%, offsets 15%, trim/extend/fillet/chamfer/break/join
15%, measurement (closest point, length, area, MASSPROP) 10%, hatch boundaries 10%,
constraints 10%.

## Numbers and tolerances (≈ 30%)

| Item | AutoCAD | CADCraft | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | IEEE double, 3D throughout | f64, **2D kernel** (`Vec2`); Z kept only on entity points and 3D polylines | `geom/src/vec.rs` |
| Tolerance model | Relative to geometry (the ACIS/AcGe tolerance context), stable at survey coordinates | one absolute `EPS = 1e-9`, plus ad-hoc absolute 1e-12/1e-14 in intersections and 1e-3/1e-4 world units for tessellating curves; a few relative tolerances (line–line denominator, hatch, solver) | `geom/src/lib.rs:26`, `intersect.rs:8,19,34,50`, `cmd/modify.rs:469-474`, `snap.rs:98-110` |
| Robust predicates | Exact orientation decisions where it matters | none | — |
| Large coordinates (UTM, 1e6–1e7) | Works | untested; absolute tolerances will misjudge tangency and coincidence, and absolute tessellation steps create huge sample counts that hit caps | — |
| Point merging (JOIN, PEDIT Join fuzz, region) | Fuzz distance per command | JOIN 1e-9 absolute; PEDIT has a fuzz; region grid-key rounding at `tol` | `modify.rs:419`, `region.rs:42` |
| Display precision (LUPREC, AUPREC, units) | Decimal, Engineering, Architectural, Fractional, Scientific; 5 angle formats | units formatting and parsing of all of them | `engine/src/units.rs` |

## Curves (≈ 60%)

| Curve | AutoCAD | CADCraft |
|---|---|---|
| Line, ray, xline | yes | yes, exact |
| Circle, arc, bulge polyline | yes | yes, exact |
| Ellipse, elliptical arc | yes | yes (center, major axis, ratio, parameters) |
| Spline: CV form, rational, any degree | yes | yes: rational B-spline, basis-function evaluation |
| Spline: fit points | degree 3 with end tangents, knot parameterisation (chord, square root, uniform), fit tolerance | cubic, chord-length, averaged knots, dense solve; **no end tangents, no knot parameterisation choice, no fit tolerance** (`geom/src/spline.rs:31-88`) |
| Spline: closed/periodic | periodic | "closed" appends the first point and refits; **not periodic** (`modify2.rs:647`) |
| Spline editing: knot insertion, split, refine, rebuild, convert to polyline | SPLINEDIT, grips | knot insertion and splitting (`curves.rs:539-622`); refine/rebuild partial |
| Helix | yes | **no** |
| 3D polyline | yes | stored and drawn; no 3D operations |
| Regions, 3D solids, surfaces, meshes (ACIS/B-rep, NURBS surfaces, subdivision) | yes | **no** (M11) |

## Intersections (≈ 40%)

| Pair | AutoCAD | CADCraft |
|---|---|---|
| line–line, line–circle/arc, circle–circle | exact | closed form, exact; tangency decided by a fixed `|disc| ≤ 1e-12·a`, so near-tangent cases depend on scale |
| line/arc–ellipse | exact (quartic) | **tessellated**: 1e-4 world units in TRIM, 1e-3 in snaps; TRIM refines with 720 samples + 60-step bisection, near-exact against line/arc cutters (`modify2.rs:1946-1995`) |
| line/arc–spline | exact to tolerance (subdivision + Newton) | tessellated as above |
| ellipse–ellipse, ellipse–spline, spline–spline | exact to tolerance | **polygon approximations** only |
| Self-intersections (curves, offset loops) | yes | **no routine** |
| Apparent intersection (projected) | yes | treated as plain intersection |

## Offsets (≈ 30%)

| Curve | AutoCAD OFFSET | CADCraft (`cmd/modify.rs:276-424`) |
|---|---|---|
| Line, ray, xline | exact | exact |
| Circle, arc | exact | exact (radius change) |
| Ellipse | spline approximation within tolerance | **a polyline** from tessellation at 1e-3 × major axis |
| Spline | spline approximation within tolerance | tessellate at 1e-3, offset vertices along normals, keep about 40 points, refit: **lossy** |
| Polyline with arcs | exact, with self-intersection trimming, OFFSETGAPTYPE (extend, fillet, chamfer) | segments offset and joined at neighbours' intersections; **arc bulges not recomputed** after endpoints move (comment at L413), **no loop cleanup**, collapsed segments not removed; OFFSETGAPTYPE only echoed |
| Options: Through, Erase, Layer, Multiple | yes | see [gaps.md](gaps.md) |

## Trim, extend, fillet, chamfer, break, join, lengthen (≈ 70%)

| Command | AutoCAD supports | CADCraft supports |
|---|---|---|
| TRIM | every curve type, quick and standard modes | line, arc, circle, polyline; ellipse and spline via sampled cutting (`modify.rs:485-656`, `modify2.rs` `trim_other`); a closed spline leaves one open spline On a closed polyline a pick before the first or after the last cut keeps the run between the cuts and nothing more (#726). |
| EXTEND | every open curve | line, arc, polyline, elliptical arc, open spline (runs on along its end tangent, `modify2/curve_edits.rs`) |
| FILLET | lines, arcs, circles, polylines, ellipses, splines, xlines, rays; Trim/No trim | lines, arcs, circles (TTR circle), polyline mode, Trim/No trim, Multiple; elliptical arcs and splines with any of these (tangent circle from sampled offsets refined by Newton's method, `geom/src/fillet.rs`; arcs trimmed or extended round the ellipse, splines split at the touch point); two straight segments of one polyline (adjacent, or with one between that the corner replaces), a polyline's straight end segment with a line (the line joins it); not polyline arc segments, xlines or rays |
| CHAMFER | lines, polylines, xlines, rays | lines, Distance/Angle, whole polylines (Polyline option), polyline segments as for FILLET (`modify2/fillet_pline.rs`); refuses arcs, ellipses and splines with a message, as AutoCAD; not xlines or rays |
| BREAK | every curve | line, arc, circle, polyline |
| JOIN | lines, arcs, polylines, ellipses, splines, helixes | line, arc, polyline into a polyline; elliptical arcs on one ellipse into a larger arc or the full ellipse (gaps close); Close turns a single arc into its circle and a single elliptical arc into its full ellipse; splines with lines, arcs, polylines and elliptical arcs into one exact NURBS (degree elevation, rational arcs; `geom/src/nurbs.rs`); no helixes |
| BREAK | every curve | line, arc, circle, polyline; a closed polyline loses the stretch from the first to the second point along its vertices and is left open (#1173) |
| JOIN | lines, arcs, polylines, ellipses, splines, helixes | line, arc, polyline into a polyline; elliptical arcs on one ellipse into a larger arc or the full ellipse (gaps close); splines with lines, arcs, polylines and elliptical arcs into one exact NURBS (degree elevation, rational arcs; `geom/src/nurbs.rs`); no helixes |
| LENGTHEN | lines, arcs, polylines, elliptical arcs, splines | line, arc, polyline; elliptical arc (arc length along the ellipse); open spline (cut along the curve, or run on along its end tangent) |

Where line and arc are supported the results are exact.

## Measurement (≈ 40%)

| Quantity | AutoCAD | CADCraft |
|---|---|---|
| Closest point: line, arc, circle, polyline | exact | exact |
| Closest point: ellipse, spline | exact to tolerance | **sampled** (`curve.rs:264`, `curves.rs:637`) |
| Tangent points, common tangents | every curve | circles and arcs only (`curve.rs:170-183`) |
| AREA: circle, ellipse | exact | exact area (ellipse perimeter by Ramanujan, not exact); an open elliptical arc has no area, like an arc |
| AREA: polyline with arcs | exact (bulge segments) | **tessellated at 1e-4** (`curve.rs:491`) |
| MASSPROP (regions: area, perimeter, centroid, moments) | exact on regions and solids | shoelace over a tessellated circle, polyline or first hatch loop (`utility.rs:310-352`); no regions |
| LIST/DIST/ID precision | full double | full double |

## Hatch boundaries (≈ 45%)

`geom/src/region.rs`: curves are polygonised, crossings split on a grid, vertices merged at
`tol`, a ray picks the edge and the face is traced by sharpest left turn; islands by
connectivity (including islands made of separate lines, #163). Caps: 60,000 segments, 4,096
islands. Missing: **gap tolerance (HPGAPTOL)**, true arcs and curves in boundaries (boundaries
come out tessellated, so a hatched circle's boundary is a polygon), island detection modes
beyond the default, boundary sets, and retained associative boundaries for every case. Pattern
lines are scanline families clipped against the tessellated loops (`render/src/hatch.rs`).

## Constraint solver (≈ 50%)

| Item | AutoCAD | CADCraft (`crates/constraints`) |
|---|---|---|
| Geometric constraints (12) | coincident, collinear, concentric, fix, parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, vertical, tangent, smooth (G2), symmetric, equal | all 12; Smooth is G2 (common point, tangent and curvature, `curves.rs`) between a spline and a line, arc, elliptical arc, polyline segment or spline; between two non-spline curves it stays tangency |
| Dimensional constraints | linear, horizontal, vertical, aligned, angular, radial, diameter; dynamic and annotational; reference | distance (aligned/horizontal/vertical), angular, radius, diameter; parameters and expressions (`expr.rs`), with one depth limit across syntax trees and parameter references |
| Geometry | lines, arcs, circles, polylines, ellipses, splines, blocks | line, circle, arc, polyline, point; ellipse and elliptical arc (centre, axis ends and arc ends as points; tangent, coincident, concentric, horizontal/vertical on the major axis); spline (fit or control points as points; tangent and smooth at its ends; open clamped or fit splines); block reference (insertion point, and the block's own points riding rigidly with position and rotation) (`model.rs`) |
| Algorithm | proprietary | damped Gauss–Newton / Levenberg–Marquardt, numeric Jacobian, per connected component; MAX_ITER 200, MAX_ROWS 800; curve–curve tangency with an ellipse through auxiliary contact parameters |
| Over-constraint | refused with a message | redundancy by Jacobian rank (Householder QR with column pivoting, rows and columns balanced), including Fix; the message names the constraints the new one duplicates; conflicts by removal probing (up to 48 probes) |
| Degrees of freedom, fully constrained state | shown (constraint bars, status) | `constraints.dof` and `constraints.inspect`: free parameters minus Jacobian rank per component, per-object DOF from the null space, under/fully/over-constrained status (`dof.rs`); a status strip on each constraint bar and the drawing's state on the canvas |
| Inference while drawing (CONSTRAINTINFER) | yes | CONSTRAINTINFER (variable and command): after a drawing or editing command, what it placed exactly onto existing geometry (snaps, ortho, polar) gets Coincident (end, mid, centre, on object), Tangent, Perpendicular, Parallel and Horizontal/Vertical, filtered by the AutoConstrain types (`auto.rs` `infer_placed`) |

## Tests

`#[test]` counts on 2026-10-10: geom 28, constraints 22, render 50, engine 174. A property-based
and hostile-input suite for geometry numerics landed 2026-10-12 (`crates/geom/src/property_tests.rs`):
a deterministic xorshift generator (no new dependency) drives a few thousand cases per property —
intersections lie on both curves and are symmetric, circle pairs match the closed form, closest
points are fixed points (perpendicular inside the segment, endpoints outside), three-point arcs
keep `{start, end} = {p1, p3}` and contain p2 (the CCW-only storage swaps the pair when p2 is on
the clockwise side, as DXF does), and hostile inputs (NaN, infinities, subnormals, raw bit
patterns, 1e300) never panic and return only finite hits or none. Known answers hold at 1e6–1e7
coordinates to 1e-9 relative.

## What to do first (ranked)

1. Exact ellipse and spline intersection and closest point (subdivision + Newton with a
   relative tolerance); use them in snaps, TRIM, EXTEND, BREAK. 15–25 h.
2. Polyline offset with bulge recomputation, self-intersection cleanup and OFFSETGAPTYPE;
   spline/ellipse offset as fitted splines within a tolerance. 15–25 h.
3. A tolerance context relative to the drawing's extents, and a known-answer test suite at
   origin and at 1e6–1e7 coordinates. 8–12 h.
4. Exact areas and MASSPROP for bulge polylines, regions (2D) and hatch loops. 6–10 h.
5. Hatch gap tolerance and curved boundaries. 8–12 h.
6. ~~Solver: DOF reporting, G2 Smooth, ellipse/spline geometry, constraint inference.~~ Done (#546).
7. Spline fit options (end tangents, knot parameterisation, fit tolerance, periodic). 6–10 h.

Total ≈ 90–140 h; items 1–6 parallelise across two or three agents.

## Revision history

| Date | Change | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-22 | minor | Constraint expressions count operator chains toward the syntax-tree depth limit; evaluation shares one depth limit across operators and parameter references, with a 1 MiB-stack regression (#1936) |
| 2026-10-14 | trivial | JOIN Close: a single arc becomes its circle, a single elliptical arc its full ellipse (#1175) |
| 2026-10-12 | trivial | TRIM on a closed polyline keeps only the complementary run when the pick lies past the last cut (#726) |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Property-based and hostile-input tests for geometry numerics landed (`crates/geom/src/property_tests.rs`): intersections, closest points, three-point arcs, bounds, vector identities; hostile f64s never panic; known answers at 1e6–1e7 |
| 2026-10-10 | major | First geometry-precision audit: tolerances, curves, intersections, offsets, modify commands, measurement, hatch, solver |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | EXTEND, JOIN and LENGTHEN on elliptical arcs and splines; closed splines trim to one piece; trim/extend section 45% → 55% (#466) |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | FILLET with elliptical arcs and splines; trim/extend section 55% → 65% (#466) |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | FILLET/CHAMFER with polyline segments (same polyline, end segment with a line); section 65% → 70% (#466) |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | Constraint solver (#546): DOF report, G2 Smooth, ellipse/spline/block geometry, CONSTRAINTINFER |

#### 💡 常见技术架构问答 (FAQ for Developers & AI Agents)

* **Q1: 如何获取 cadcraft 的最新生产级部署拓扑与权威镜像源？**

### Hardware parity

# Hardware parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-13 · **Change:** minor (zoom and pan regenerate in the background) · **Target:** Autodesk AutoCAD 2027 (Mac and Windows)

The hardware AutoCAD uses and how CADCraft compares, per platform. Work items:
[gaps.md](gaps.md#hardware).

**Headline (estimated): hardware ≈ 45%.** 2D GPU drawing, HiDPI and trackpads are covered on
every platform. Missing: 3D mice, tablets/digitizers, GPU-accelerated 3D (there is no 3D), and
any deliberate multi-monitor handling. Remaining: **≈ 15–25 Opus 5.5 hours**, plus a human with
the devices to test 3D mice and tablets.

Measured from the source on 2026-10-10 (`crates/ui-egui/src/gpu.rs`, `canvas.rs`,
`apps/cadcraft/src/graphics.rs`, `apps/cadcraft-web`); AutoCAD's side from Autodesk's system
requirements and graphics-performance documentation. Nothing was benchmarked in this pass.

| Feature | AutoCAD 2027 | CADCraft macOS | CADCraft Windows | CADCraft Linux / FreeBSD | CADCraft web |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU canvas for 2D | yes (hardware acceleration, GPU smoothing, high-quality geometry) | wgpu on Metal | wgpu on DirectX 12 by default (`WGPU_BACKEND` overrides; GL avoided after AMD crashes, #31) | wgpu on Vulkan (or GL) | WebGPU, WebGL2 fallback |
| CPU fallback | software mode | yes (`tiny-skia` rasteriser) | yes | yes | — |
| GPU for 3D (shaded visual styles, ray-traced rendering) | yes | no (no 3D) | no | no | no |
| Low-latency presentation | yes | vsync or low-latency via `CADCRAFT_VSYNC` | same | no vsync queue so the crosshair keeps up (#183) | browser-controlled |
| HiDPI / Retina, display scaling | yes | yes (egui points per pixel) | yes; a Windows 11 DPI fix is queued upstream (PR #110) | yes | yes |
| Multi-monitor (palettes on other screens, per-monitor DPI) | yes | not handled deliberately; one window | same | same | — |
| Trackpad pan, pinch zoom | yes (Mac) | yes, with trackpad vs wheel detection (#58) | wheel only (precision touchpad untested) | wheel; delay reported on Linux Mint (#25) | browser events |
| Magic Mouse | yes | treated as a trackpad | — | — | — |
| Wheel mouse, middle-button pan | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse) | yes | **no** | **no** | **no** | no |
| Pen tablet / digitizer (TABLET command, calibration) | yes (Windows) | **no** | **no** | **no** | no |
| Screen magnifier following the cursor | yes | — | breaks (#39; PR #187 adds a system-cursor option) | — | — |
| Plotters and printers (PC3 devices, system printers) | yes | **no**: PDF/PNG/SVG files only; Print asks where to save the PDF (#26) | same | same | PDF bytes shown instead of a download (#134) |

## Performance on hardware (internal numbers only)

From the earlier roadmap (measured by the agents that built it, 2026-10-06, `cadcraft-cli perf`):
200,000 entities pick in 0.001 ms, about 4 ms after an edit (incremental R-tree), and the GPU
canvas draws a frame in about 4 ms. Nothing has been compared with AutoCAD on the same machine,
and 1M-entity drawings are untested. A 10 MB DWG took about two minutes to fail (#57).

Zoom and pan no longer freeze the window (2026-10-13). On a hatched 12k-entity architect's DWG
(about 340k display primitives) each zoom step used to block the UI for 2–4.5 s while the
display list, its vertex data and its GPU buffers were rebuilt. These rebuilds now run on a
worker thread while the previous list is drawn, so the longest stall is 26–64 ms (M-series Mac).
Edits still rebuild on the UI thread (about 1.8 s on that drawing): per-entity caching is the
next step.

## Revision history

| Date | Change | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-13 | minor | Zoom and pan regenerate in the background: 2–4.5 s stalls down to 26–64 ms on a hatched DWG |
| 2026-10-10 | major | First hardware parity doc: GPU backends per platform, input devices, displays, plotters |

### Localization parity

# Localization parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-22 · **Change:** minor (the command line enables the OS IME and handles composition/commit, so single-line TEXT edits accept CJK input; previously: Brazilian Portuguese row updated and terminology reviewed; previously: Swedish catalog completed with the 95 strings added since; previously: Swedish catalog added: complete catalog, menu headings, native-speaker terminology review; previously: complete current Korean catalog with Hangul font coverage) · **Target:** Autodesk AutoCAD 2027 for Mac (26.0)

How far CADCraft's interface and drawing text are from AutoCAD's languages. Summarised in
[ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md#languages); work items in [gaps.md](gaps.md#localization).

## What the target ships

Measured from the installed AutoCAD 2027 for Mac bundle by listing only (folder names, nothing
read): `Contents/Resources` has `Base.lproj` (English), `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `ja`, `ko` and
`zh_CN` localizations, and `Resources/Support` has matching `@de@` … `@zh_CN@` folders. That is
**8 interface languages** on the Mac. AutoCAD for Windows also has language packs for Traditional
Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Polish, Czech and Hungarian (Autodesk's published
language-pack list, not measured here). AutoCAD's spell checker ships about 20 dictionaries
(`*.dct` names in `Resources/Support`).

Drawing text in AutoCAD: TrueType and SHX big fonts (CJK), Unicode `\U+` escapes, complex-script
shaping and right-to-left text through TrueType, vertical SHX text styles.

## What CADCraft has

- **A display-time string catalog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/`, landed with #36): a TSV per
  language (context, English source, translation, `@plural` rows), Edit → Interface Language with
  Auto (system language), live switching, a saved choice, and tests for coverage, placeholders
  and plurals ([localization.md](localization.md)). The Ukrainian and German catalogs have
  **989 rows** each,
  covering menus, command labels, tool groups and tooltips, the Start page, tabs, status
  controls, object snaps, drafting prompts, property labels and dialogs. Engine diagnostics,
  CLI/MCP responses and command history stay English, and uncatalogued text falls back to
  English. For scale: about 1,160 unique capitalised string literals exist in `crates/engine`
  and `crates/ui-egui` (grep, 2026-10-10).
- **Drawing text:** TrueType/OpenType/`.ttc` through `skrifa` with per-character font fallback
  and FONTALT, so CJK characters render (#173). DXF text is written with `\U+` escapes so
  non-ASCII survives in R2000 files (#169). Lines with right-to-left text get the Unicode
  Bidirectional Algorithm and OpenType shaping with `harfrust` (Arabic, Persian and Urdu joining,
  lam-alef, ZWNJ, marks; Hebrew), in TEXT and MTEXT including wrapping (#287). Left-to-right lines
  are still placed one glyph per code point: **no shaping** for Devanagari and other Indic
  scripts, and **no vertical text**. SHX fonts are not read; our stroke font stands in.
- **Text input:** egui/winit IME. The command line — which collects single-line TEXT edits and
  other prompt text — now enables the operating system IME while a prompt asks for text and shows
  composition (pre-edit) text until it is committed, so Chinese, Japanese and Korean input works
  there (#1761); egui's own text fields handle IME themselves. Several upstream IME fixes are
  queued as PRs (#110–#119: macOS Korean, emoji picker, Windows caret placement, X11 and Wayland),
  so CJK input is not yet reliable on every platform.

## Languages

Order and columns from craftrules' progress-docs standard. Every UI percentage is **measured**
from the catalogs (0 rows for every language without a catalog file). Hours are **estimated**:
about 3–5 h per language for an Opus 5.5 agent to translate the ~990 catalog rows and fix layout,
plus native review by a human; extending the catalog to the remaining English-only strings
(engine diagnostics, uncatalogued text) is about 4–6 h, counted once in the first row.

| Language | Code | UI strings translated | Dialogs / tooltips / help | Script support | Native review | Status | Estimate to `full` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| English | en | source (100%) | 100% (help is a command reference, not AutoCAD-sized help) | Latin: yes | n/a | full | — |
| Simplified Chinese | zh-Hans | 0 (0%) | 0% | CJK glyphs render via fallback; IME fixes pending (#110–#119); no vertical text | no | none | 8–12 h (includes extending the catalog, 4–6 h) |
| Spanish | es | 0 (0%) | 0% | Latin: yes | no | none | 3–5 h |
| Hindi | hi | 0 (0%) | 0% | Devanagari: no shaping | no | none | 3–5 h + 15–25 h shaping (shared with Arabic) |
| Arabic | ar | 0 (0%) | 0% | Drawing text shaped and laid out right to left (#287); the UI is not mirrored | no | none | 3–5 h + 15–25 h RTL UI |
| French | fr | ≈ 900 catalog rows (gaps reported, English fallback) | partial | Latin: yes | contributed by @pechnikov2026-star (#624); no native review yet | partial | 2–4 h |
| Russian | ru | ≈ 900 catalog rows (gaps reported, English fallback) | partial | Cyrillic: yes (bundled egui fonts) | contributed by @pechnikov2026-star (#624); no native review yet | partial | 2–4 h |
| Portuguese (Brazil) | pt-BR | 1,231 catalog rows; reference catalog and marked UI literals covered (no gaps reported) | dialogs and tooltips yes; command reference searchable in Portuguese | Latin: yes (bundled egui fonts; accented letters tested) | catalog by @WladmirJunior, completed with AI assistance by @RicSchonfelder; terminology reviewed by a native speaker (@ffishman) | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | line-by-line proofreading + shared English-only UI work |
| Indonesian | id | 0 (0%) | 0% | Latin: yes | no | none | 3–5 h |
| Japanese | ja | 0 (0%) | 0% | CJK glyphs render; IME pending; no vertical text | no | none | 4–6 h |
| German | de | 989 catalog rows (≈ 100% of the catalog; ≈ 80% of all UI strings, estimated: engine diagnostics and uncatalogued text stay English) | dialogs and tooltips yes; command reference searchable in German | Latin: yes (bundled egui fonts cover ä ö ü Ä Ö Ü ß; long strings will need layout checks) | no native review | partial | 1–2 h |
| Greek | el | 1,330 catalog rows (all collected existing source keys) | Menus, dialogs, tooltips, drawing prompts, command labels and contextual headings; English fallback for uncatalogued UI | Greek script; bundled egui glyph check added | Original AI-assisted translation by @Camthalion77, independent native review pending | complete current catalog; uncatalogued UI remains English | native proofreading and platform layout review |
| Korean | ko | 1,235 rows (1,229 ordinary, 4 menu, 2 count); full existing catalog union and marked UI coverage | dialogs, tooltips, Options and translated command-reference labels | UI requires catalog-covering installed or optional craft-fonts Hang/Kore face; English fallback without one; IME fixes still pending | original AI-assisted translation; independent native proofreading pending | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | native review + platform layout/IME validation |
| Vietnamese | vi | 0 (0%) | 0% | Latin with stacked diacritics: renders per code point, untested | no | none | 3–5 h |
| Ukrainian | uk | 989 catalog rows (≈ 100% of the catalog; ≈ 80% of all UI strings, estimated: engine diagnostics and uncatalogued text stay English) | dialogs and tooltips yes; command reference searchable in Ukrainian | Cyrillic: yes (bundled egui fonts) | translated by a contributor; no second review | partial | 2–4 h |
| Czech | cs | 1,202 catalog rows; reference catalog and marked UI literals covered | dialogs and tooltips yes; contextual menu headings; command reference searchable in Czech | Latin: yes (bundled egui proportional and monospace fonts; Czech letters and quotes tested) | AI-assisted by @Losminek; independent review pass; not yet proofread by a native speaker | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | native review + shared English-only UI work |
| Swedish | sv | 1,330 catalog rows; reference catalog, marked UI literals and menu headings covered (no gaps reported) | dialogs and tooltips yes; contextual menu headings; command reference searchable in Swedish | Latin: yes (bundled egui proportional and monospace fonts; å ä ö é and Swedish quotes tested) | AI-assisted (Claude Code) by @holmbom; terminology and the running app reviewed by a native speaker | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | line-by-line proofreading + shared English-only UI work |
| Italian | it | 1,227 catalog rows; reference catalog and marked UI literals covered | dialogs and tooltips yes; contextual menu headings (Visualizza / Vista, Edita / Modifica); command reference searchable in Italian | Latin: yes (bundled egui fonts; accented letters tested) | AI-assisted by Emanuele Bottelli (Claude), written from the English strings with Italian desktop-CAD vocabulary; no native proofreading pass yet | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | native review + shared English-only UI work |
| Hungarian | hu | 1,326 catalog rows; reference catalog, marked UI literals and menu headings covered (no gaps reported) | dialogs and tooltips yes; contextual menu headings; command reference searchable in Hungarian | Latin: yes (bundled egui proportional and monospace fonts; ő ű Ő Ű and the other accented letters tested) | translated by @Skaywalker from the English strings; independent native proofreading pending | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | native proofreading + shared English-only UI work |
| Turkish | tr | 1,330 catalog rows; reference catalog, marked UI literals and menu headings covered (no gaps reported) | dialogs and tooltips yes; contextual menu headings (Ölçülendirme / Ölçü); command reference searchable in Turkish | Latin: yes (bundled egui proportional and monospace fonts; Ç Ğ İ Ö Ş Ü ç ğ ı ö ş ü tested) | AI-assisted by @ogzhnklvz, written from the English strings with Turkish desktop-CAD vocabulary; the running app reviewed by a native speaker | complete current catalog; English-only interface gaps remain | line-by-line proofreading + shared English-only UI work |

Other languages shipped: Ukrainian, Brazilian Portuguese, German, Czech, Russian, French, Italian, Korean, Swedish, Hungarian and Turkish.
Czech, Swedish, Hungarian and Brazilian Portuguese cover the reference catalog and every marked UI literal; engine diagnostics and uncatalogued text
remain English. AutoCAD for Mac ships 7
non-English languages (zh-Hans, es, fr, ja, de, ko, it); of those, CADCraft now ships German and Korean,
and additionally Ukrainian, which AutoCAD for Mac doesn't ship.

**Total to put all twelve at `full`:** about 55–95 Opus 5.5 hours (catalog extension 4–6 h,
ten translations 30–50 h, complex-script shaping and RTL 30–45 h), plus native-speaker review for
each language, which needs humans. Translations parallelise fully once the catalog exists.
